about: Likely capacity energized by year, 2025 to 2030: bottom-up from the tracker's sites (ESTIMATE)
Every number here is an Estimate. It is built from the tracker's rows (sourced rows only, same rows as the published totals) as of 16 Nov 2026.

How it works: each row has a stage (Operating, Under construction, Permitted, Paper). The Assumptions sheet gives each stage a chance of happening and how likely it is to arrive on its stated year, one year late or two years late.

(2) A spending cut by year is then applied to every row not yet operating: the reported SemiAnalysis capex cut on US rows, half of it elsewhere (both editable). Likely GW for a row in a year = row GW x chance of happening x share arriving in that year x (1 - that year's cut). The yellow cells on Assumptions are inputs: change them and every sheet recalculates.
Rows dated in a year that has already passed without the site operating are moved to the stage's earliest possible year. Undated rows get the stage's default year.
Operating rows dated after 2026 (the unbuilt part of a partly live site) are treated as Under construction. Paused or delayed rows have their own stage.

Sheets: Summary (by year, stage, region, with the SemiAnalysis cross-check), By chip maker, By end user, By operator (facility GW), Rows (one line per site phase or unsited agreement remainder, with live formulas).
Units: facility GW unless a column says IT. IT GW is the tracker's IT figure (facility / PUE where not stated).
Chip maker, end user and operator follow the tracker's counting rules: a known vendor is always assigned (A8); an end user marked ESTIMATED is the tracker's estimate (B8).
Not the published totals. The tracker's published totals count everything announced (rule A1); this workbook is a separate view of what is likely to energize.
